title: Pakistan’s 3.2% export growth masks a deeper value-chain problem
summary:
Pakistan’s textile and apparel exports across HS 50-63 rose 3.2 per cent to $7.52 billion in the first five months of 2026.
Cotton (HS52) was the fastest-growing major category, up 11.5 per cent to $1.10 billion, with China accounting for 94 per cent of the increase.
The rise was driven by cotton yarn, not finished fabric, while knitwear, filament yarns and staple-fibre products weakened.

title: Bangladesh para-tariffs double effective border protection: World Bank
summary:
Bangladesh’s border protection averages 15.4 per cent with para-tariffs, versus a 7.0 per cent trade-weighted MFN tariff.
Footwear, hides and skins and transport equipment among others face the widest gaps, shaping sourcing and pricing.
The World Bank urges phased cuts and says full reform would cost 0.83 percentage points of GDP.

title: ICE cotton futures rise ahead of WASDE amid supply concerns
summary:
ICE cotton futures ended a five-session slide, with December 2026 settling at 87.28 cents, up 0.98 cent.
US crop condition worsened as good/excellent ratings fell to 34 per cent, keeping supply concerns in focus before Friday’s WASDE.
China’s State Reserve sold 8,007 tonnes in its 38th sold-out auction, while domestic ZCE cotton stayed weak.

title: Is polyester's crude-led rally sustainable amid weak demand?
summary:
Global polyester feedstock markets firmed in the first week of September 2026 as US-Iran tensions lifted crude oil, PTA and MEG.
PTA rose across major routes, with CFR India up 1.6 per cent and CFR Southeast Asia up 2.8 per cent between August 31 and September 4.
MEG gains were sharper, led by domestic China up 13.5 per cent, but weak downstream demand left polyester makers nursing wider losses.

title: World Bank urges Bangladesh to cut tariffs ahead of LDC graduation
summary:
World Bank has advised Bangladesh to phase down tariffs, remove para-tariffs and negotiate deeper trade agreements as LDC graduation approaches.
For apparel, footwear and input-dependent manufacturers, lower duties could improve sourcing costs but reduce border-tax protection.
The study warns abrupt reform could hit import-tax revenue, so fiscal and worker-adjustment measures are needed.

title: Indian minister Goyal urges BRICS push for women-led exporters
summary:
Indian minister Piyush Goyal has urged BRICS to expand opportunities for women-led enterprises in global trade through easier credit, buyer access and predictable rules.
For textile and apparel exporters, proposed BRICS platforms, e-documents and sectoral women-led delegations could widen market links.
Goyal also pushed action on invoice discounting, exhibitions and a Women’s Advancement Fund up to 2030.

title: Barmag to showcase POY 2.0 under ‘A New Era’ at ITMA Asia 2026
summary:
Barmag will showcase next-generation spinning, texturing, staple fibre and nonwoven technologies at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai.
Led by POY 2.0, the portfolio combines automation, digital process control, energy savings and flexible production.
Solutions including atmos.io, eFK EvoSmart, EvoSteam, FiberGuard and hycuTEC target higher productivity, lower waste and more sustainable textile manufacturing.

title: Will Europe's 25 ppb fluorine limit set a new textile standard?
summary:
EU REACH Entry 79 becomes binding on October 10, 2026, for specified clothing, accessories and footwear, with 25 ppb and 1,000 ppb PFHxA limits.
A wider EU restriction covering more than 10,000 PFAS is in ECHA assessment; SEAC is due to finalise its opinion by end-2026.
EU-bound suppliers need testing, traceability and documentation; other consumer textiles come into scope on October 10, 2027.

title: Bangladesh, Hong Kong sign Investment Promotion & Protection Agreement
summary:
Bangladesh and Hong Kong signed an IPPA at the 11th Belt and Road Summit 2026 in Hong Kong on September 9.
The pact aims to protect investors and capital from both sides and formalise the investment environment.
Hong Kong, Bangladesh’s seventh-largest investment source, is expected to channel more capital into readymade garments, textiles and other potential industries.

title: Bangladesh, US review trade & investment conditions
summary:
US envoy Brent T Christensen told Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir that US companies are keen to operate in Bangladesh.
The talks covered investment, bilateral trade, energy co-operation, import policy changes and transparency in large infrastructure projects.
For sourcing teams, the discussion points to continued focus on market access, energy supply and business-process reform.

title: US' Lands' End returns to profit as Q2 revenue rises to $302 mn
summary:
Lands' End returned to Q2 FY26 profit, with net income of $3.5 million as revenue rose 2.7 per cent to $302.0 million.
US e-commerce led growth, rising 9.0 per cent to $182.4 million; Outfitters gained, while third-party sales dropped 20.4 per cent.
Lands' End reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with inventory up 13 per cent for seasonal build as operations normalised before the holiday season.

title: US apparel imports are weak; so why did bookings jump 79%?
summary:

Clothing and accessories-store sales rose 5.9 per cent to $151.09 billion; June's inventory-to-sales ratio fell to 2.14.
US-bound HS61–62 ocean bookings reached 21,434 TEU in June, up 79 per cent, led by Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Australia’s apparel imports dip 7.5% in July 2026
summary:

Fibre imports edged up to Au$12 million, while textile fibre exports declined 9.92 per cent to Au$629 million, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.
Fiscal 2025–26 saw apparel imports down 4.60 per cent and fibre exports up 7.72 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s RMG sector bets on technology for a productivity edge
summary:
Bangladesh apparel exporters are adopting digital monitoring, data-driven production and AI tools to raise productivity, reduce downtime and improve quality.
Some factories report gains of up to 25 per cent versus manual monitoring, though results vary by technology, conditions and measurement.
The shift also raises concerns over worker pressure, privacy and fair sharing of productivity gains.

title: Jordan’s clothing exports rise 1.8% to $1.19 bn in H1 2026
summary:
Jordan’s apparel and clothing accessory exports rose 1.8 per cent year on year to JOD 846.6 million (~$1.19 billion) in H1 2026.
Knitted apparel grew 3.0 per cent to JOD 830.7 million and made up more than 98 per cent of clothing exports.
Woven apparel exports fell 36.4 per cent, while knitted and woven apparel imports rose 2.4 per cent in H1.

title: RMG exports from B’desh in green zone as shipment jumps in August 2026
summary:
Bangladesh's RMG exports rose 5.12 per cent to $7.495 billion in July-August 2026, backed by a strong August, EPB provisional data show. 
Knitwear grew 6.17 per cent to $4.193 billion, while woven apparel increased 3.81 per cent to $3.301 billion. 
Home textile exports gained 11.17 per cent to $154.55 million, but cotton and cotton products fell 13.02 per cent to $82.24 million.

title: As Sri Lanka’s exports grow, is apparel losing momentum?
summary:
Sri Lanka’s combined merchandise and services exports reached $10.49 billion in January–July 2026, up 5.48 per cent year-on-year. 
Apparel and textiles fell 6.50 per cent to $2.88 billion, diverging from broader export growth. 
July apparel and textile exports dropped 8.8 per cent to $437.59 million, with shipments declining across the United States, European Union and United Kingdom.

title: A meeting that highlights the fraying edges of Bangladesh’s RMG story
summary:
BGMEA told the President that nearly 400 garment factories have closed in Bangladesh over three years, as production costs rose almost 40 per cent. 
Inadequate gas supplies, higher energy tariffs, wages and bank interest rates are forcing many factories to operate below half capacity. 
Garment exports contracted 1.64 per cent in FY2025-26 and fell 1.92 per cent in July of FY2026-27.

summary:
